pairs.distinction: Fighting at home is conflict; not feeling safe with someone is fear of being hurt, and may need crisis resources first.
pairs.reason: Someone afraid for their safety needs to find that pain without wondering whether ordinary family fights are the same thing.

pairs.distinction: Struggling with a partner is a hard relationship; not feeling safe is about danger, and the person may not be a partner.
pairs.reason: Folding danger into relationship trouble would hide a sensitive pain inside an everyday one.

pairs.distinction: Loneliness is the overall feeling of being alone; the other is wanting company for going out.
pairs.reason: Someone can have close people and still have no one to go out with, so a person can choose between them, more easily if the loneliness line is made concrete.

pairs.distinction: Loneliness is day-to-day isolation; no one to lean on is having nobody to call in a crisis.
pairs.reason: Plenty of people with a busy social life have no one they'd call at 2am, and the fixes differ.

pairs.distinction: Belonging is about fitting into a group or place; loneliness is about missing people day to day.
pairs.reason: People often feel they don't fit in anywhere while still having a few friends, so the two read differently.

pairs.distinction: Belonging is never having found a place; the other is losing one you had.
pairs.reason: Losing a community you had is a grief of its own, but the two currently share the name Belonging, which the alternatives fix.

pairs.distinction: Dating is about finding a partner; intimacy is missing closeness, which people in relationships feel too.
pairs.reason: Someone married can miss closeness without wanting to date, so the two are easy to tell apart.

pairs.distinction: Relationship strain is conflict or difficulty with a partner; intimacy is missing closeness, with or without one.
pairs.reason: A calm relationship can lack closeness and a close one can be full of fights, so neither covers the other.

pairs.distinction: Dating is wanting a romantic partner; loneliness is missing people in general.
pairs.reason: Many people want a partner without feeling alone, and many feel alone without wanting to date.

pairs.distinction: New in town has a clear cause and its own fixes (meeting neighbors, local groups); loneliness can last for years with no move.
pairs.reason: Someone who just moved will recognize their situation right away, and the fixes for it are specific.

pairs.distinction: New in town is knowing nobody where you live; the other is lacking company for going out, even among people you know.
pairs.reason: Knowing nobody at all and knowing people who don't invite you are different situations.

pairs.distinction: This is losing a specific community you belonged to; loneliness is missing people in general.
pairs.reason: Leaving a church or other close community is a loss people name on its own.

pairs.distinction: Interests is about finding people who share a passion; the other is about having company at all.
pairs.reason: Someone with plenty of friends can still have no one who loves what they love.

pairs.distinction: Drifted apart is losing touch with particular friends; loneliness is the overall feeling of being alone.
pairs.reason: Missing old friends is specific enough to choose without thinking twice, and the fix is reaching back out.

pairs.distinction: Relationship is trouble with a partner; family is fighting among the people you live with, often parents, kids or siblings.
pairs.reason: The conflict involves different people, so someone can tell which one is theirs.

pairs.distinction: Caregiving is looking after a sick, disabled or aging person; parenting is raising your own kids.
pairs.reason: Most people would not call raising their kids caregiving, and the help available is different.

pairs.distinction: Caregiving names the cause; no time of my own can come from work, kids or anything else.
pairs.reason: Caregiving takes far more than time, so it stands as its own pain on People.
Being worn out raising kids is personal, while the cost of childcare is a shared problem, so each belongs on its own page with a link between them.
